findings.explanation: Each append subsearch ends in `stats count`, so it returns one row; the row cap never limits how many notables are counted. append also has its own maxout (default 50000) separate from limits.conf; the real risk is the 60-second maxtime auto-finalize, which silently undercounts.
findings.quote: default `subsearch_maxout` (ten thousand) can clip a high-volume `` `notable` `` `append` if your estate generates more than the cap in thirty days; raise `maxout` under `limits.conf` `[subsearch]`
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with: long-running append subsearches are auto-finalized after maxtime (default 60 s), which truncates the counted events; set `append maxtime=` explicitly or pre-aggregate notable counts into a summary index.

findings.explanation: The ITSI-documented macro for pulling full KPI rows from itsi_summary is `get_full_itsi_summary_kpi(<kpi_id>)`; `get_full_kpi_summary` is not a documented ITSI macro. The same wrong name appears in dataSources.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `` `get_full_itsi_summary_kpi(<kpi_id>)` `` in both detailedImplementation and dataSources, or query `index=itsi_summary` with `indexed_itsi_kpi_id::<id>` directly.

findings.explanation: multisearch only accepts streaming subsearches; every append block here ends in `stats`, so the suggested swap would fail as written.
findings.quote: long `append` chains run subsearches serially; for sub-second dashboards, shift to `multisearch`
findings.suggested_fix: Recommend the summary-index collector approach (already mentioned) and drop the multisearch suggestion, or state that each subsearch must be reduced to streaming commands before multisearch and the stats moved after it.

findings.explanation: The ITSI summary index reference documents `kpi` (KPI title), `alert_level`/`alert_severity`, `alert_value` and `health_score`; `kpi_name` may not be a documented itsi_summary field.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the ITSI summary index reference for the KPI-title field name and use `kpi` and `alert_value` if `kpi_name` is not listed; recommend `alert_level` for filtering, as the doc does.

findings.explanation: The scenarios refer to `span=1h`, `host` grouping, synthetic probes and onboarding baselines. None of these exist in a monthly aggregate heatmap with no host or span. The real causes are already in detailedImplementation Step 5: threshold recalibration, thin NPS samples, quarter-end pull-forward, ESCU enablement spikes, and stale feeds.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the KFPs from the Step 5 causes (threshold_version change, NPS response_count < 30, quarter-end revenue artefacts, newly enabled ES content inflating notables, missing snow:incident feed) and remove the host/span text.

findings.explanation: The reviewer is an automated agent (`agent-handcraft-2026-04-28`) and nothing records SME sign-off, yet the SPL has logic defects (see the SLA-ratio flag).
findings.suggested_fix: Set status to a non-verified state until a named SME validates the SPL against live data.

findings.explanation: Nothing in the UC uses Cisco ACI data; the `cisco` equipment tag is likewise unsupported by any data source.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove `cisco_aci` from equipmentModels and `cisco` from equipment.

findings.explanation: The SPL's lookup outputs only green_threshold, amber_threshold and direction, and the final table drops threshold_version, so the panel cannot show it without SPL changes.
findings.suggested_fix: Note that `threshold_version` must be added to the lookup OUTPUT and table, or remove it from the panel description.

findings.explanation: This count appears in detailedImplementation Step 2 and does not match the SPL, which has six append subsearches.
findings.quote: so dashboards do not re-run seven subsearches on every page load
findings.suggested_fix: Say six subsearches, or 'each domain subsearch'.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: SLA breach rate is computed on events already filtered to `sla_breached="true"`, so `breached` counts all breached incidents while `total` counts only breached-and-not-closed ones. The ratio is meaningless and can exceed 100%. The base search should drop the breach filter and use `count(eval(sla_breached="true")) AS breached, count AS total`.

The metric labelled `DSO` is `avg(days_overdue)` of open invoices. That is not Days Sales Outstanding (AR / revenue × days), and it goes negative for invoices not yet due. Likewise `NPS Score` is `avg(score)` of 0–10 responses, not promoters minus detractors. The thresholds and board labels will be misread; rename the metrics (e.g. 'Avg Days Past Due', 'Avg Survey Score') or compute the true formulas.

`sla_breached` is not a standard ServiceNow incident column (the incident table exposes `made_sla`; breach detail lives in `task_sla.has_breached`). Check the Splunk Add-on for ServiceNow `snow:incident` field list before relying on this filter.

The leading `| inputlookup business_risk_thresholds.csv` rows have no `value`, so `where isnotnull(value)` removes them all; the inputlookup does nothing and makes the search harder to read. Start with the first subsearch (or `makeresults`) instead.

summary: The detailed implementation and data-source text are substantive and mostly accurate, but the SPL has a broken SLA-breach ratio and mislabelled DSO/NPS metrics, the troubleshooting advice misstates append/subsearch limits and multisearch behaviour, the ITSI macro name is wrong, and the templated sections (description, value, KFP, evidence, controlTest) describe a different detection.
